videos.script: Every chart that uses colour uses a palette, and there are only three kinds. {{three}} The first separates things: regions, products, payment methods. It needs colours that look different and equally important. {{categorical}} The second orders amounts, from low to high. It needs one direction of lightness, light to dark, and nothing else. {{sequential}} The third shows two sides of a middle: above and below target, growth and decline. It needs two colours that meet at a pale centre. {{diverging}} Most bad colour on charts is the wrong kind of palette for the data. A rainbow on a heatmap of sales. A diverging scale on a column of counts. Five shades of one blue for five unrelated products. {{wrong}} This lesson shows each kind, the rainbow that every tool used to offer first, and how to find good palettes in the tools you already have. {{plan}}
